extracted.intended_audience: scientists, members and organisers of scientific congresses, and readers of Nature
extracted.subtask_description: Provisional programmes, logistics, and organisational suggestions for scientific meetings (International Zoological Congress and British Association sectional meeting), plus recommendations for validating an astronomical theory.

rubrics_metrics.name: Time-table visibility at sectional meetings
rubrics_metrics.description: Outside each sectional meeting there should be a time-table board showing what precisely is going on.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Practical organisational recommendation to place a visible schedule near meeting rooms so attendees can immediately see the programme for that section; suggested as one of two practical improvements from experience.

rubrics_metrics.name: Participant identification by numbered badge
rubrics_metrics.description: Each member should wear in his button-hole a number corresponding to a printed list, so that strangers to one another may know at once who's who.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Simple identification system (numbered badges linked to a printed list) to facilitate networking and recognition among delegates; given as a recommended practice for large congresses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Excursion participation threshold and cost arrangements
rubrics_metrics.description: If fifty members agree to go there will be an excursion to Bermuda; expenses for each participating member will be thirty-two dollars for return passage and about two dollars a day hotel charges while in Bermuda.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sets an explicit minimum-participation threshold (50) to run optional excursions and provides a clear cost breakdown; notes that after landing the local committee will supply transport and incidentals free of charge and that facilities for collecting/preserving zoological material will be provided.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provision of daily hospitality during congress week
rubrics_metrics.description: On each day of the strict congress week there will be luncheon at the invitation of the local committee, and the evenings will be occupied with receptions and dinners.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Expectation that host/local committee will arrange generous daily hospitality (luncheons, evening receptions/dinners) for delegates; an organisational norm for the described congress.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sectional programme composition and activities
rubrics_metrics.description: Sections are to include presidential addresses, arranged discussions (including joint discussions between sections), contributed papers and communications, committee reports, demonstrations, exhibits, excursions, and special lectures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Enumerates the types of programme items expected in a well-rounded scientific section (examples drawn from many sections: mathematical/physical sciences, chemistry, geology, zoology, geography, engineering, anthropology, physiology, botany, education). Encourages joint meetings on cross-cutting topics and inclusion of excursions and demonstrations where appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Validation requirement for Kapteyn's two-drift theory
rubrics_metrics.description: Kapteyn's theory, which accounts for the anomalous distribution of stellar motion directions, is still awaiting the verdict of spectroscopic determinations of line-of-sight velocities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: States that spectroscopic line-of-sight velocity measurements are the appropriate empirical test for the two-drift theory; notes that sufficient material/data exist and that investigators with access to such data should carry out the test.

rubrics_metrics.name: Methodological note on determining the solar apex from proper motions
rubrics_metrics.description: The two-drift theory allows determination of the solar apex from the directions of proper motions only; this method is free from assumptions about stellar distances but has a large probable accidental error and does not represent an absolute motion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Highlights trade-offs of a method: advantage (no distance assumptions) versus disadvantage (large accidental errors); cautions against confusing the derived 'solar motion' with motion relative to the aether.
